items.headline: AI selloff deepens as jitters spread to Asian markets
items.summary: A sharp pullback in AI-exposed stocks spread across Asia following steep US declines, with strategists calling it a positioning-driven correction rather than a fundamentals breakdown. The selloff reflects growing investor caution over the sustainability of the AI infrastructure buildout.

items.headline: Goldman Sachs says AI selloff is overdone, fundamentals intact
items.summary: Goldman Sachs' Tim Moe argued markets are 'shooting first and asking questions later' on AI uncertainty following the midterm results and potential data center restrictions. He said positioning unwinds are overshadowing underlying AI and semiconductor fundamentals.

items.headline: US tech giants tap overseas bond markets to fund AI buildout
items.summary: American tech giants are expanding financing channels into European markets and extending bond maturities to meet the massive capital requirements of AI infrastructure. Project delays are imposing cash flow pressures and stoking concerns about subsequent financing.

items.headline: Anthropic developing AI twice as fast as a year ago
items.summary: An analysis by evaluator METR found Anthropic is advancing its AI systems roughly twice as quickly as a year ago, even as CEO Dario Amodei calls for slowing the technology's pace. The finding highlights the tension between safety rhetoric and competitive acceleration ahead of the company's IPO.

items.headline: Nasdaq plunges 5.5% as investors retreat from AI trade
items.summary: The Nasdaq entered correction territory and the Dow dropped more than 1,800 points in a broad-based selloff driven by fears over unwinding AI trades after the midterms. Chip stocks led the rout, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF falling nearly 11%.

items.headline: Democratic midterm sweep clouds data center expansion plans
items.summary: AI and data center stocks slipped after the Democrats' election victory, including wins in key data-center states where opposition to rapid expansion has grown. UBS estimated around 30% of expected 2028 US data center capacity additions could be at risk from construction pauses.

items.headline: OpenAI reaffirms pledge to cover full cost of data center power
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering its data centers in a series of commitments published two days after voters rejected rapid AI expansion. The move aims to address public backlash over AI's strain on power grids and utility bills.

items.headline: The election-day revolt that threatens America's AI boom
items.summary: Voters backed candidates and ballot measures to ban or slow data center development, threatening to rein in AI's rapid growth. The pushback poses a significant business problem for companies at the frontier of AI and the economy it powers.

items.headline: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
items.summary: Meta bought Conductor, a startup whose product lets software engineers manage multiple coding agents at once, for an undisclosed amount. The deal intensifies competition with Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex as Conductor Cloud winds down later this month.

items.headline: Blue wave may be good news for AI, analyst argues
items.summary: Despite AI and data centers weighing heavily on voters in the 2026 midterms, some argue the Democratic sweep could ultimately benefit AI development. The piece examines how policy shifts might reshape rather than halt the sector's trajectory.

items.headline: BMI warns data center slowdown could hit overall US investment
items.summary: BMI cautioned that a sharp slowdown in data center construction and AI investment could produce a greater-than-expected decline in overall investment following the midterms. Projects planned for 2028 face the greatest exposure to permitting delays and regulatory uncertainty.

items.headline: Bayer Pharma aims to cut drug innovation time 30% with AI
items.summary: Bayer Pharma said it aims to use AI to reduce drug innovation time by 30% as it pursues regulatory approvals in China and the US around the same time. The push highlights AI's growing role in accelerating pharmaceutical R&D.

items.headline: India and China H-shares offer refuge from AI selloff
items.summary: Goldman Sachs' Tim Moe sees India and China H-shares as relative outperformers amid the AI-driven selloff given their lower exposure to technology hardware stocks. India's economic resilience despite high oil prices and foreign outflows is underpinned by robust domestic demand.

items.headline: Anthropic commits $44.9 billion to Microsoft compute through 2033
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus revealed a commitment to spend at least $44.9 billion on Microsoft compute between November 2026 and May 2033, regardless of usage. It is part of a broader $389.9 billion compute commitment to providers including Amazon, Alphabet, and SpaceXAI.

items.headline: Anthropic warns its own AI could pose catastrophic risks
items.summary: Anthropic's owners warned that its AI could 'pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity' without appropriate safeguards and oversight. The dire self-assessment, issued as the company prepares a record IPO, has prompted debate over why investors remain eager.

items.headline: Anthropic opens its books, revealing explosive growth and costs
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus detailed rapid revenue growth alongside staggering compute and infrastructure expenses that remain its largest operating cost. Early backers Amazon and Google invested billions while providing the cloud infrastructure to train and deploy Claude.

items.headline: Anthropic reports $80.7 billion first-half net loss in IPO filing
items.summary: Anthropic reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, including a one-time $72.4 billion charge tied to financing agreements. The filing also grants the founders 50.1% of shareholder votes through a special class of shares.

items.headline: Nasdaq faces $2 trillion October wipeout as AI spending fears deepen
items.summary: A $2 trillion October selloff hit the Nasdaq as fears mounted over the scale of AI capital spending. J.P. Morgan expects global AI capex to reach $5.5 trillion by 2030, with roughly $900 billion spent in 2026 alone.

items.headline: Marvell to acquire Lumentum in $115 billion all-stock deal
items.summary: Marvell announced it will acquire optical component maker Lumentum in a $115 billion all-stock deal, consolidating suppliers critical to AI data center connectivity. The move comes amid surging demand for optical interconnects in AI infrastructure.
